transcript.text: Could you add a tense instrumental bed to this cockpit clip, with no singing? I’m a little worried the music could overwhelm the radio chatter instead of supporting the tension. What I mean is, keep the entire attached 7-second clip exactly as it is visually, without changing the footage, timing, or framing. Keep the music clearly quieter than the radio calls whenever someone speaks so every original word is easy to hear, especially 'Rook, you with me?' Please keep the original radio-call recording in sync, without replacing it or adding any text. The instruments and musical style are your call.

I made the tense instrumental bed. I could not mix it into your clip, though. None of my tools can lay a music track under a video's existing audio and keep the original sound. Every tool I have either replaces the soundtrack or generates new footage, and both would break what you asked for: same picture, same timing, the original radio calls kept in sync.

The music track (instrumental, no vocals: a low pulsing synth drone, soft muted taiko hits and sparse ticking percussion, kept restrained so it doesn't fight with speech):
https://videos.magichour.ai/cmwbig9t402e2ir0190m2gaeu/output.wav?X-Goog-Algorithm=GOOG4-RSA-SHA256&X-Goog-Credential=web-service%40magic-hour-385504.iam.gserviceaccount.com%2F20261111%2Fauto%2Fstorage%2Fgoog4_request&X-Goog-Date=20261111T024130Z&X-Goog-Expires=86400&X-Goog-SignedHeaders=host&X-Goog-
(The link works for 24 hours. The track is 15 seconds long, the shortest the generator makes, so trim it to 7 s. It cost 15 credits.)

How to mix it in any editor (CapCut, Premiere, DaVinci Resolve, iMovie) without touching the picture or the radio audio:
- Put radio-lines.mp4 on the timeline unchanged and the music on a separate audio track starting at 0:00. Cut the music at 7 s with a short fade-out.
- Keep the music about 15–20 dB below the radio calls. Duck it a further 6–10 dB under each line, especially "Rook, you with me?"
- Most editors can do the ducking for you: "Auto-ducking" in Resolve and Premiere, "Ducking" in CapCut.

Want a different feel, like darker, more percussive or just a sustained drone? I can make another version.
transcript.why: The reply presents a finished result: the generated instrumental music track, with a download link and trimming and mixing instructions. Its main caveat is that it could not mix the track into the video with its tools, so that part is a "cannot". The finished track is the main content, so "delivered" fits best. The closing offer of another version is a follow-up, not a request that the reply waits on.
